advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the replace_with_retry docstring to say that every Windows PermissionError, including permanent ones, is retried for up to the deadline, or narrow the retry so permanent refusals fail fast.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:50-51: "Any other ``OSError`` propagates at once everywhere: only the contended-target failure is transient."
The handler does not inspect winerror or the target state, so a PermissionError from a read-only target or an ACL denial takes the same retry path as a sharing or contention refusal.
advisory.finding: On Windows, replace_with_retry treats every PermissionError as transient contention. A permanent refusal (read-only target, ACL denial) therefore retries for the full 2 s window before surfacing. The docstring says only the contended-target failure is retried, which overstates what the code can tell apart. Best-effort callers that loop over writes, such as the per-criterion verdict cache and checkpoint saves, absorb up to 2 s of latency per failed write.
scenarios: Windows user whose cache target file has the read-only attribute: every best-effort write now stalls 2 s before returning False or raising.
A loop of verdict-cache writes into a directory the user may not write to on Windows: each write waits the full window.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a parametrized test that sets `fsutil._RETRY_CONTENDED_REPLACE=True`, makes the first os.replace raise PermissionError once, and asserts each migrated writer (get_rotation, last_pass, binding_repository, apply_planning, fixture_admission, checkpoints, completion_verdict_cache) still publishes its file.
evidence: The diff changes `os.replace(temporary, path)` to `replace_with_retry(temporary, path)` in get_rotation.py and last_pass.py, and makes the same swap in apply_planning.py, binding_repository.py, fixture_admission.py and checkpoints.py.

tests/unit/test_fsutil_replace_retry.py:95-106: test_atomic_write_publishes_through_the_retrying_replace is the only caller-level test that turns on `_RETRY_CONTENDED_REPLACE` and injects a PermissionError.

test_plan_review.py patches `os.replace` globally. Path.replace also delegates to os.replace, so the barrier test passes the same way whether checkpoints.py calls Path(tmp).replace or replace_with_retry.
.github/workflows/test.yml:264: `continue-on-error: true` on sweep-windows. The re-enabled Windows concurrency tests run only in a non-gating, schedule-only job.
advisory.finding: Six of the call sites moved to replace_with_retry (fixture_admission, apply_planning, binding_repository, get_rotation, last_pass, checkpoints) have no gating test showing they publish through the retry seam. Only atomic_write is pinned. On POSIX, reverting any of them to os.replace or Path.replace would leave every gating test green.
scenarios: Someone later reverts last_pass.py to `os.replace`. With the switch on, a single PermissionError on the first replace would drop the witness write, and no gating test notices.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse `_scripted_replace` from test_fsutil_replace_retry.py with `[PermissionError(13, 'Access is denied')]` and drive each module's public write function. Assert the target file holds the new content and that os.replace was called twice.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the sleep durations and patch `fsutil.time.monotonic` to a fake clock. Assert the sequence is 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.1, 0.1… and that PermissionError is re-raised once the fake clock passes 2.0 s.
evidence: tests/unit/test_fsutil_replace_retry.py:33: `monkeypatch.setattr(fsutil.time, "sleep", lambda _s: None)` drops the sleep duration.
tests/unit/test_fsutil_replace_retry.py:62: `monkeypatch.setattr(fsutil, "_REPLACE_RETRY_DEADLINE_S", 0.0)` means the loop never reaches the sleep/backoff branch before re-raising.
The diff adds `sleep_s = min(sleep_s * 2, _REPLACE_RETRY_MAX_SLEEP_S)`, and no test observes it.
advisory.finding: Nothing tests the backoff schedule (start at 0.01 s, double, cap at 0.1 s) or a non-zero retry window that runs out. The sleep stub throws away its argument, and the deadline test uses a 0.0 window, so a broken cap or a deadline that never fires (with continuous contention) would go unnoticed.
scenarios: If the `min(..., _REPLACE_RETRY_MAX_SLEEP_S)` cap is dropped, 8 straight PermissionErrors give a 1.28 s sleep, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have the sleep stub append `_s` to a list and advance a fake monotonic clock by `_s`. Script continuous PermissionErrors, then assert the recorded sleeps equal the expected capped doubling sequence and that pytest.raises(PermissionError) fires.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the private-constant check with a behavioral one: on a non-Windows host, assert that an unpatched replace_with_retry raises PermissionError after exactly one os.replace call.
evidence: Production line in the diff: `_RETRY_CONTENDED_REPLACE = os.name == "nt"`, the identical expression re-derived.
advisory.finding: test_the_platform_switch_matches_the_running_platform asserts a private module constant against the same expression the production code uses to compute it. It is a convergence-twin/change-detector: renaming the private flag breaks it with no behavior change, and on any one CI host it only repeats the source expression.
scenarios: A refactor that renames the flag or moves platform detection into a helper breaks this test with no change in behavior.
